strengths: The paper presents a clean, self-contained Bayesian derivation of a metaplastic gated linear attention mechanism, with full free-energy derivations, closed-form updates, and the diagonal-approximation steps clearly documented in Appendices A.2–A.6.

The unifying framework (Table 1) that recovers Longhorn, (Gated) Deltanet, MesaNet, and Palimpsa as different posterior approximations of a common objective is genuinely insightful, and the observation that Mamba2 emerges as an asymptotic special case where forgetting dominates is a useful conceptual contribution.

The Mamba2-to-Palimpsa continuum is exploited practically: the reparameterization (v*_t = β_t ⊙ v_t with b_scale) allows pre-trained non-metaplastic models to be fine-tuned into metaplastic ones at matched token budgets, which is a sensible and economical training pipeline.

Experiments include systematic ablations of metaplasticity (w/o Meta variants) on both a synthetic MQAR benchmark (8 seeds, learning-rate search, curriculum) and 170M/760M pre-training on FineWeb-Edu, allowing the effect of metaplasticity to be isolated from other architectural differences.

The paper is transparent about limitations: it honestly reports training-throughput overheads (1.5x–3x vs Simple GLA), register-pressure bottlenecks of the chunk-wise kernel, exclusion of MesaNet due to unstable public code, and the compute trade-offs of the fine-tuning strategy. The limitations and efficiency analysis (Appendix A, Fig. 5) are unusually candid.

Learning-dynamics analysis (Fig. 3) provides mechanistic evidence that the model actually uses metaplasticity (memory window growth, ~40x plasticity differentiation) rather than the mechanism being inert.
weaknesses: Novelty is incremental: Palimpsa is essentially the MESU weighted-posterior method (Bonnet et al., 2025) applied to linear attention with a diagonal precision approximation, closely paralleling Longhorn's approximation. The resulting update rule (Eq. 5) is a simple elementwise gated recursion, and the paper does not clearly delineate what is new beyond transposing MESU into this setting.

Empirical gains are modest and partly confounded. At 170M, the fully trained Palimpsa variants do not beat Gated Deltanet; the headline results come from fine-tuned variants. At 760M the improvement over Gated Deltanet is ~0.8 average accuracy points, within the range where seed and evaluation variance matter, and no significance analysis is provided for Table 2 (unlike MQAR's 8 seeds). Palimpsa-D w/o Meta already outperforms Gated Deltanet at 760M, so architectural changes beyond metaplasticity contribute to the headline numbers.
The claim that 'Mamba2 is a special case of Palimpsa' is asymptotic and approximate (|I−I_prior|/I_prior ≪ 1), not an exact reduction; the framing in the abstract is stronger than what is derived.

The weighted-posterior construction (Eq. 8–9) replaces the exact truncated-posterior forgetting term with a geometric-mean proxy whose quality is not analyzed or empirically validated; the VI 'recovers the exact solution' only before the diagonal approximation, after which the Bayesian interpretation is heuristic.

Evidence for the long-context capacity claim is thin: language evaluation uses Wikitext/LAMBADA and standard commonsense benchmarks at ≤760M scale; no needle-in-a-haystack or long-context retrieval experiments at realistic sequence lengths are reported, despite this being the central motivation.

Transformer++ remains competitive or superior on several metrics (e.g., best HellaSwag/PIQA/WinoGrande at 170M), so the practical significance of the metaplastic gains relative to a strong dense baseline is not established.

No explicit statement of code release; given the custom Triton kernel and nontrivial fine-tuning protocol (b_scale schedule, checkpoint selection), reproducibility would currently rely on appendix descriptions alone.

strengths: The variational free-energy derivation is clean and provides a genuinely useful unifying lens: Table 1 casts Longhorn, (Gated) Deltanet, Mesa, and Palimpsa as different posterior approximations of a common objective, and the observation that Mamba2 emerges as an asymptotic special case where forgetting dominates is an interesting conceptual contribution.

The derived update rule (Eq. 5 / A.5) is concrete, closed-form, and implementable; the chunk-wise associative-scan kernel (Appendix A.8, Eq. 33) shows the method is deployable at scale rather than purely conceptual.

Experiments go beyond synthetic toy settings: real pre-training at 170M and 760M on FineWeb-Edu (15B/30B tokens) with commonsense-reasoning evaluation, plus MQAR with 8 seeds, learning-rate search, and error bars — a level of rigor often missing in this line of work.

The fine-tuning pipeline (converting a pre-trained Mamba2/Deltanet into a metaplastic model via the v* = βt ⊙ vt reparameterization) is a practical and cleverly motivated contribution enabled by the theory.

Honest treatment of limitations: register-pressure bottlenecks, 1.5–3× training slowdown, 4× kernel-level inference slowdown, and the exclusion of MesaNet due to numerical instability are all disclosed rather than hidden.
weaknesses: Empirical gains are modest and the headline claims are overstated. 'Consistently outperforms baselines' is not well supported: at 760M the average advantage over Gated Deltanet is ~0.8 points with several per-task losses (e.g., HellaSwag), and at 170M, Transformer++ (43.80) essentially matches fine-tuned Palimpsa-D (43.96) while Palimpsa-D fully trained underperforms (43.45). The paper's strongest architecture is only the fine-tuned variant, which makes the practical recipe more fragile than the abstract suggests.

The novelty relative to MESU (Bonnet et al., 2025) is limited: the weighted-posterior forgetting mechanism, the metaplasticity framing, and much of the machinery are inherited directly from MESU; the contribution is essentially porting MESU to linear attention with a diagonal covariance approximation. The diagonal approximation is a substantial restriction that weakens the 'per-synapse metaplasticity' story (per-column rather than truly per-parameter plasticity, given kt is shared across rows).

The Mamba2 'special case' result is asymptotic and approximate (|I−Iprior|/Iprior ≪ 1), achieved via a specific reparameterization that fixes βt near zero; presenting it as an equivalence overstates the result.

The Bayesian interpretation of the forgetting gate is loose in practice: Nt is first derived as a memory window, then immediately reparameterized as αt = exp(−A dt) with learnable A, so the claimed 'Bayesian interpretation of the effective dependency range' is more narrative than enforced by the model.

Theoretical approximations are accumulated without error analysis: replacing the truncated posterior by the weighted posterior (A.2, Eq. 8–9), assuming pw ≈ q from the previous step, and then the diagonal approximation — the final update could plausibly be justified by much weaker assumptions, leaving unclear what the Bayesian framing buys beyond Longhorn's heuristic gating.

Reproducibility is only partial: hyperparameters and initialization are commendably detailed, but no code or kernel release is mentioned in the manuscript, and the custom Triton kernel is the central engineering artifact.

Compute overhead is significant (3× training slowdown at 760M) and the promised compensation — that inference is fast — is only shown for the isolated attention kernel at B=1 on an RTX 3090, not end-to-end model throughput; the efficiency claim in the abstract ('scales efficiently on GPUs with speeds comparable to Mamba1') is not demonstrated.

Missing ablations/analyses: no comparison against MESU itself, no analysis of whether the learned importance state I actually identifies 'important' content in language modeling (the metaplasticity-ratio analysis in Fig. 3 is only on MQAR), and MQAR differences at L=1024 have overlapping error bars.

strengths: The paper offers a coherent and largely complete theoretical unification: gated linear attention models (Longhorn, Deltanet, Gated Deltanet, Mesa, and asymptotically Mamba2) are derived as special cases of a variational free-energy objective under different posterior approximations (Table 1, Appendices A.2–A.6). The derivations are worked out in detail and the closed-form updates follow cleanly.

The derived update rule is genuinely deployable: the authors built a fused Triton kernel with chunk-wise associative scanning (A.12) and honestly quantify its costs (1.5–3× training slowdown, ~4× inference slowdown vs. Simple GLA), which is rarer than claims of 'comparable speed'.

The fine-tuning recipe (Section 2.4) converting any pre-trained Mamba2 into a metaplastic Palimpsa via the bscale reparameterization is a clever and practically useful contribution, exploiting the theoretical Mamba2-as-limit-case result rather than leaving it as analysis only.

Evaluation spans multiple scales (MQAR with 8 seeds and LR search; 170M/760M pre-training on 15B/30B tokens; 2.7B model surgery on a 300B-token Mamba2 checkpoint) with controlled token budgets for fine-tuning comparisons, and the baseline receives the identical 2.7B training recipe.

The limitations discussion is unusually candid: fully-trained Palimpsa-D underperforming its fine-tuned variant, RULER regressions at short contexts (VT drops from 59.6 to 33.5 at 4k), Aggregation task degradation, and register-pressure bottlenecks are all reported rather than hidden.
weaknesses: The practical gains on language modeling are modest and mixed: average commonsense accuracy improvements of ~0.6–0.84 points, with several individual tasks worsening (e.g., LMB ppl and Winogrande for Palimpsa-M at 170M, LMB ppl regressing at 2.7B after fine-tuning), and no variance/significance reporting for the language benchmarks (unlike the 8-seed MQAR setup).

The long-context story is not cleanly supported: on RULER the metaplastic model substantially underperforms at 4k–16k and only wins at 32k on one subtask (VT), while the baseline dominates most Retrieval and all Aggregation tasks (Table 6); the claimed 'expansion of memory capacity' rests on per-token NLL curves and a narrow set of results.

The Bayesian framing is partly narrative rather than load-bearing: in the conjugate setting VI recovers the exact posterior anyway (as the authors admit), the final model uses a diagonal approximation admittedly 'stronger than mean-field', and the forgetting mechanism is imported from MESU (Bonnet et al., 2025). The net novelty over Longhorn/Mesanet is a per-synapse diagonal importance state plus MESU-style forgetting, which is incremental.

Important baselines are missing from the language experiments: Titans, TTT, and other test-time-training/memory-augmented models are discussed in related work but not compared; Mesanet is excluded citing numerical instability, leaving the most similar metaplastic competitor unevaluated.

Reproducibility is weakened by an empty code link ('Our code is available at' followed by no URL), which is a notable omission for a paper whose contribution depends on custom kernels; hyperparameters in the appendix partially mitigate this.

The 2.7B 'model surgery' result (replacing 8 of 64 layers chosen by measured memory window) is interesting but under-analyzed — no ablation of layer count/placement, and the selection heuristic's generality is unclear.

strengths: The unifying Bayesian framework is the paper's most valuable contribution: Table 1 cleanly derives Longhorn, Deltanet, Gated Deltanet, Mesa, and Palimpsa as specific choices of stability matrix, input gating, and posterior approximation, and the observation that Mamba2 emerges as a limiting case where forgetting dominates is insightful and actionable.

The derivation is technically careful: the closed-form variational updates (Appendices A.2–A.5) are worked through in detail, the diagonal precision approximation is explicitly flagged as stronger than a standard mean-field assumption, and the connection to MESU and Aitchison et al.'s neuroscience model is well motivated.

The empirical program is unusually thorough for this line of work: ablations with metaplasticity disabled (equivalent to Mamba2/Gated Deltanet), two backbones, three scales (170M, 760M, 2.7B with a 300B-token pretrained checkpoint), 8 seeds with error bars on MQAR, and a controlled fine-tuning budget (metaplastic variants fine-tuned from the same checkpoints with matched token budgets).

The limitations are treated with unusual honesty: the paper acknowledges that fully trained Palimpsa-D underperforms its fine-tuned counterpart, that Palimpsa regresses on RULER VT at short contexts (4k–16k), that aggregation tasks degrade, and quantifies the kernel overhead (1.5×–3× training, ~4× inference slowdown vs. Simple GLA).

The fine-tuning/continuum result (Section 2.4) has practical value: showing that a pretrained Mamba2 can be converted to a metaplastic model via bscale reparameterization, plus layer-wise surgical replacement guided by measured memory windows Nt, is a genuinely useful recipe.
weaknesses: The headline empirical gains are small and statistical support is thin. Improvements of +0.6–0.8 average accuracy points at 760M and +0.84 at 2.7B are within typical run-to-run variance for these benchmarks, yet the language modeling and commonsense results appear to be single runs with no significance testing or confidence intervals (only the MQAR experiments have 8 seeds). Given that the abstract claims Palimpsa 'consistently outperforms baselines,' the evidence for the LM experiments is not proportionate to the claim.

The Bayesian narrative is partially disconnected from what is actually trained. The final algorithm rests on several stacked approximations (weighted-posterior proxy in Eq. 8–9, diagonal precision, bscale reparameterization that 'fixes βt arbitrarily close to zero'), and the fine-tuning procedure is essentially an engineering trick to interpolate toward Mamba2. The paper does not test whether the probabilistic quantities (importance, uncertainty) behave as the theory predicts beyond the qualitative Fig. 3 dynamics.

Key comparisons are missing. Mesanet is excluded due to 'numerical instabilities' in third-party code (understandable but leaves the closest methodological competitor—full-covariance metaplasticity—unbenchmarked), and Titans / other test-time-training models are absent. The generative claim that the framework 'unifies' gated models would be stronger with at least one derived-but-not-previously-tested variant validated empirically.

Reproducibility is undermined by an incomplete artifact: the Code Availability section contains an empty URL ('Our code is available at' with no link). For a paper whose contributions include custom Triton kernels and a multi-stage fine-tuning pipeline, this is a material gap.

The 2.7B experiment is a single model surgery on one checkpoint with absolute LongBench scores around 19–20, suggesting a weak operating regime where relative comparisons may not generalize; there is also no ablation of the number of replaced layers or the layer-selection criterion.

Some presentation issues reduce clarity: the forgetting gate is parameterized as αt = 1 − 1/Nt but also as exp(−Adt) without spelling out the exact correspondence between the two parameterizations; Fig. 3 is referenced before its content is fully defined; and Fig. 2 differences between methods are visually small relative to the seed variance shown.

strengths: The unification framework (Table 1, Sec. 2.3, Appendices A.3–A.6) is genuinely valuable: deriving Deltanet, Gated Deltanet, Mesa, Longhorn, and Mamba2 as special cases of a variational free-energy objective over an attention memory provides real conceptual insight into why gated linear models take their current form, and makes the 'Mamba2 as a forgetting-dominated limit' observation precise and actionable.

The metaplasticity mechanism is well-motivated and the derivation is clean: the free-energy decomposition into plasticity/forgetting/stability terms (Eq. 3) transparently connects neuroscience-inspired metaplasticity (Aitchison et al.) to concrete update rules, and the weighted-posterior trick for in-context forgetting is a neat, differentiable solution avoiding growing memory or task labels.

The empirical program is unusually comprehensive for this line of work: synthetic MQAR with 8 seeds and curriculum, pre-training at 170M/760M on 15-30B tokens, and a 2.7B 'model surgery' experiment on a pre-trained Mamba2 checkpoint with a properly matched baseline recipe (A.10), which directly tests the practical fine-tuning pipeline the theory motivates.

The fine-tuning reparameterization (Sec. 2.4, bscale) is a thoughtful bridge between the theory (Palimpsa-M reduces to Mamba2) and practice, allowing cheap non-metaplastic pre-training followed by metaplastic fine-tuning without full retraining.

The per-token NLL analysis (Fig. 4) and the RULER Variable Tracing degradation curves at 32k (24.4 vs 14.9) provide evidence for the central claim (expanded memory capacity) beyond aggregate accuracy, and the appendix honestly reports where the method underperforms (single-needle retrieval, aggregation tasks, short contexts).

Limitations are discussed candidly (slower training than fully trained counterparts, register-pressure bottlenecks, 1.5-3x training overhead, 4x inference slowdown vs Simple GLA in A.12-A.13), and the authors resist overclaiming in those sections.
weaknesses: The headline empirical gains are small and somewhat fragile: ~0.6-0.8 points average accuracy at 760M, +0.84 at 2.7B, and the abstract's claim that Palimpsa 'consistently outperforms baselines' is contradicted by the paper's own data (e.g., fully trained Palimpsa-D underperforms Gated Deltanet at 170M with worse WikiText ppl; RULER VT is worse at 4k-16k; CWE/FWE aggregation degrades). The narrative 'consistently' needs to be tempered to match Table 2 and Table 6.

The efficiency story is internally inconsistent with the main text: the introduction claims 'speeds comparable to Mamba' with custom kernels, but Appendix A.12/A.13 admit 1.5-3x slower training than GLA and ~4x slower inference than Simple GLA. The claim should be reconciled; as written, the main text overstates scalability.

The 2.7B long-context results rest on a single surgical configuration (8 of 64 layers replaced) with no ablation of the number/choice of replaced layers, no error bars, and the LongBench gain (+1.1 overall, driven by 'medium') coexists with a short-category decline (18.9 to 16.1), so the long-context benefit claim would benefit from more runs and sensitivity analysis.

Reproducibility is undermined by an empty Code Availability section ('Our code is available at' with no URL). Given that the contribution depends on custom Triton kernels and a multi-stage fine-tuning pipeline, this is a material gap. Appendix hyperparameter tables partially mitigate this but do not substitute for released code.

The theoretical novelty should be situated more carefully: the view that linear attention is online gradient descent/Bayesian regression (Akyurek et al., Von Oswald et al.) and the memory-window-based forgetting are established; the incremental novelty over MESU and Mesanet is the diagonal importance state and vector beta_t. The paper argues this avoids per-row fixed plasticity, but does not empirically isolate the benefit of diagonal (per-element) importance vs. per-row plasticity beyond architectural ablations.

Language modeling experiments at 170M/760M lack seed variance reporting, and 'fine-tuned from 14BT/28BT' vs 'fully trained' budget parity is handled well, but the fair-comparison claim would be stronger with error bars as in the MQAR experiments.

Minor presentation issues: Sec. 3.4 cites 'Fig. 3' where it apparently means the layer-wise N_t analysis (Fig. 6), and the manuscript appears to have leftover template artifacts (empty code link), suggesting the camera-ready needs a careful pass.
